newsitem.title: GERMANY: Cautious start for German shares before U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Cautious start for German shares before U.S. data.

text.p: The promise of key U.S. data in the afternoon weighed on German shares in early bourse trade Tuesday, as the strong dollar prevented any serious decline but failed to enliven the market.
The 30-share DAX index, which tracks trade in German blue-chip stocks, was down 9.02 points at 2,985.51 points at 1024 GMT.

Banks, Monday's fastest advancers, were the biggest losers after third-ranked commercial bank Commerzbank AG released a disappointing net profit figure for 1996, sending its shares down 1.40 marks to 42.40 marks.
Commerzbank reported 1996 profit of around 1.19 billion marks, up 22 percent but below analysts' forecasts for 1.3 billion marks.

"Commerzbank was certainly a bit disappointing and we're going to see people taking profits on all the banks now," said a Frankfurt dealer, noting that Moody's move to downgrade Japanese banks this week was adding to pressure on bank shares.
Deutsche Bank AG, which announced an unchanged dividend for 1996, erased its gains from Monday to drop 1.65 marks to 83.50 marks.
Export-driven shares such as Daimler-Benz AG were the morning's outperformers, a fact dealers attributed to the dollar's move above 1.65 marks, auguring improved profits for German exporters.
Daimler was up 30 pfennigs at 114.30 marks.
After a slow start, engineering company Siemens AG was up 22 pfennigs at 78.80 marks as the market took a positive take on its report of a drop in first quarter net profit.
The main figure was in line with forecasts and one dealer noted that underlying foreign order figures were strong.

But the the broader market, the main focus of the day was U.S. employment cost data due at 1330 GMT -- an hour after bourse trade closes in Frankfurt -- which are expected to provide key clues on U.S. inflation.
"Nobody will want to commit themselves before then," a dealer said.
